Hallgrímskirkja, Iceland

If glaciers and rugged cliffs could form a cathedral, it would look like Hallgrímskirkja. Standing tall as Reykjavik’s most iconic landmark, this striking church defines Iceland’s architectural identity.

Constructed gradually between 1945 and 1986, its 74-meter frontage draws inspiration from the country’s basalt columns and the deep fissures of ancient glaciers — as though the landscape itself sculpted the building.

From the viewing platform at the top, panoramic views unfold across Reykjavik, the endless Atlantic, and distant volcanic ridges. Inside, minimalist design and natural light create a serene atmosphere — a quiet echo of the untamed beauty beyond its walls.

Located in central Reykjavik, the church is just a 10–20 minute stroll through picturesque streets and a short climb uphill (it sits atop a gentle slope).

💬 Defeated enemy must leave the region in disgrace: Iranian commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA –  Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, deputy chief of the Iranian Army for Coordination, referring to the US-Israeli imposed war, says the enemies must leave the region after facing disgrace and humiliation at the hands of the Iranian Armed Forces.

At a ceremony of Army non-commissioned officers (NCO) on Sunday, Sayyari, while commemorating the "Sacred Defense Week," stated that as the enemy had failed to achieve its objectives during the eight-year Iran-Iraq War, it failed again not only to achieve its sinister goals, but was met with disgrace and humiliation in the two recent wars.
​
Attributing the triumph and victory over the aggressors to the path of the martyrs and the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, he highlighted the heavy responsibility borne by new Army personnel in defending the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
​
He congratulated the Iranian nation, especially the families of martyrs who sacrificed their souls and bodies during the fight against the Iraqi Ba’athist regime. "The enemy sought to undermine Iran’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity but failed completely because of the unity of the Iranian people," Sayyari reiterated.
​
They were the ones who stood firm, baring their chests to the danger; throughout the eight years of the Sacred Defense and the subsequent imposed wars, they stood valiantly, never bowed their heads, and rubbed the enemy's nose in the dust, he lauded the martyrs.
​
Congratulating the NCO cadets on their rank-insignia ceremony, he said their mission rests on three key pillars: defending the country's territorial integrity; defending the country's independence; and preserving the sacred system of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
​
"You must follow in the footsteps of those who, over the past 48 years since Iran's glorious Islamic Revolution, have successfully carried out this mission," he noted and encouraged the young cadets to be equipped with knowledge, expertise, skills, faith, piety, courage, initiative, and creativity.
​
Rear Admiral Sayyari, recalling the Army's missions during the Sacred Defense, also pointed to evolving battlefield tactics that he said necessitate changes in combat arenas and advances in intelligence, communications, weaponry, and munitions.
​
He further emphasized the unbreakable bond between the Army and the people, saying the Army sacrifices itself for the nation, and the nation remains the Army's refuge. "The nation takes pride in having supported all the Army's missions—and indeed all missions of the armed forces—to this day," Sayyari noted.

2.1mn sq m of the country’s 5mn sq m of modern warehouses have been destroyed, with 900,000 sq m alone hit in recent months, according to Ruslan Shostak, a Ukrainian entrepreneur and founder of the Eva and Varus retail chains.

🌍 159 Iranian prisoners repatriated from Iraq: Iranian judicial official

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Justice Ministry has announced the repatriation of 159 Iranian prisoners from Iraq following joint efforts with the Judiciary and the Foreign Ministry.

The announcement was made by Deputy Justice Minister for Human Rights and International Affairs Askar Jalalian on Sunday.
​
“The Secretariat of the Committee for the Transfer of Convicts at the Ministry of Justice, in cooperation with other relevant bodies, including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Judiciary’s International Affairs Office, and the Khuzestan Province Justice Department, facilitated the transfer of 159 Iranian prisoners from prisons in Iraq to Iran,” he said.
​
Jalalian added that the number of Iranian prisoners held in Iraq has increased recently due to a rise in the number of Iranians traveling to the Arab country. He said failure to comply with Iraq’s laws and regulations, as well as the country’s strict response to violations, had also contributed to the increase in the number of Iranians being convicted in Iraq.
​
“Complying with the laws of the destination country and respecting its regulations are essential when traveling abroad. Failure to do so can result in arrest, lengthy prison sentences, hefty fines, and irreversible consequences for individuals and their families,” he noted.
